description: single pole IIR alpha = 0.02 on real samples vs single_pole_iir_filter_ff

fixed_vs_float.rationale: Coefficients rounded to Q15 change the impulse response by ||dh||_1 = 4.083659869736903e-4 (times the input peak 0.555), and each output rounding (0.5 LSB of Q15, plus 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference) is shaped by the feedback 1/A(z), ||g||_1 = 50.02748091603043: <= 32.46038230495562 Q15 LSB per component. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Coefficients rounded to Q15 change the impulse response by ||dh||_1 = 4.083659869736903e-4 (times the input peak 0.555), and each output rounding (1.0 LSB of Q15, plus 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference) is shaped by the feedback 1/A(z), ||g||_1 = 50.02748091603043: <= 57.474122762970836 Q15 LSB per component. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Coefficients rounded to Q17 change the impulse response by ||dh||_1 = 1.2475469737416317e-4 (times the input peak 0.555), and each output rounding (0.5 LSB of Q17, plus 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference) is shaped by the feedback 1/A(z), ||g||_1 = 50.00839374284627: <= 8.539868085429685 Q15 LSB per component. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

float_vs_gnuradio.rationale: GNU Radio keeps the state in double, this is f32: each step rounds the sum (terms of total size 0.5549999999999998) by 4 * 2^-24 at most, amplified by ||1/A(z)||_1 = 49.99999999999983: 0.2168 Q15 LSB. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.
